pr_title: Wayland: Restore tablet support and handle multiple tools
pr_body:
Fixes #88333.

This code was already partially there, although heavily incomplete and nowadays commented out.

It got broken after the `WaylandThread` refactor and I didn't bother to bring it over, preferring to `#if 0` it into oblivion for the time being as I don't have a tablet/pen which support an eraser and tilt reporting.

This commit brings it back and adds proper multi-tool support (needed for eraser detection) thanks to @winston-yallow, who could test this code with their more capable tablet.

---

I also noticed some occasional weird segfaults even without even having a tablet installed which I haven't been able to isolate/replicate reliably, so I'm not able to tell if they're a new thing or not.

Although it has been confirmed that eraser and tilt are properly reported now, considering the above, some further testing would be wise.

Here's a nice lil' visualizer I quickly made for this PR, please give it a spin if you have a drawing tablet: https://github.com/riteo/godot-tablet-visualizer

(I wonder if we could make this a demo or something, it's real nifty :D )
pr_comments:
> (I wonder if we could make this a demo or something, it's real nifty :D )

I think it makes sense to submit to https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects, so it can be used as a troubleshooting tool like we do with the Joypads demo.

@akien-mga

> I didn't check in detail but the memnew/memdelete stuff around TabletToolState probably needs some caution to avoid double-free or memory leaks (it's good to remember that if it needs to be freed after use, any ERR_FAIL kind of early return need to ensure it gets freed first too).

Should be good to go already I think, as if there's no godot state set (e.g. libdecor or whatever messing around with our display) it should return `null`, noopping.

We also `memdelete` their state only while getting entirely rid of their reference, so we should be fine I think.

I am trying to be as careful as possible on keeping state memory handling as easy and simple as possible without needing full RAII wrappers and whatnot.

> Should be good to go already I think, as if there's no godot state set (e.g. libdecor or whatever messing around with our display) it should return `null`, noopping.

Is `memdelete(nullptr)` safe? I see we have an unused `memdelete_notnull` macro. We often do `if (thing) memdelete(thing);` if there's a possibility for the `thing` to be null.

> Edit: wait, what about `memdelete_not_null`?

Since it was never used in the codebase, I think for now we should just do the `if (thing) memdelete(thing);` and discuss with the core team what to do more generally with this pattern.

We could refactor the whole codebase to use `memdelete_not_null`, or drop the macro and keep doing things ad hoc, or evaluate whether it would be that bad to just add a null check in `memdelete` itself.
Should be ready. I can't build it locally right now (low on battery), so a last test would probably be wise.

I built and tested af273a1efde392b4ca479b285df5d3047d9504a0 + the hotfix to bring back `tool` (which you then committed as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/af273a1efde392b4ca479b285df5d3047d9504a0..b01a36b3cd04499d959bbd169dec719e088a420a), so I pretty much tested the latest version of this PR already, ahead of its commit date :P

Also out of battery (AAAA, who uses those anymore aside from Ubisoft...) for my touchscreen pen so I couldn't actually check that the feature works :)

issue_context.title: [Wayland] Godot doesn't register inputs from graphic tablet on GNOME
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible only in v4.3.dev3.official [36e943b6b], since it's first version that introduced Wayland support.

### System information

Fedora Linux 39.20240214.0 (Silverblue), Linux 6.7.4-200.fc39.x86_64, AMD Radeon RX 570 Series, GNOME 45.4 on Wayland session, tablet in use Wacom One Pen Display 13, Forward+ renderer

### Issue description

Godot editor with enforced Wayland `run/platforms/linuxbsd/prefer_wayland = true` completely ignores inputs from Wacom tablet on Wayland session, including clicking and moving with pen. Same happens with running projects with `display/display_server/driver.linuxbsd = wayland`. With this options turned off, everything works as expected.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Change `run/platforms/linuxbsd/prefer_wayland` in editor setting to `true`.
2. Restart Godot.
3. Now Godot won't accept any inputs from tablet via pen.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Same could be achieved with running projects.
1. Create empty project.
2. Change project setting `display/display_server/driver.linuxbsd` to `wayland`.
3. Add node and attach script:
```gdscript
extends Node

func _input(event):
	print(event.as_text())
```
It generate properly generates inputs with mouse:
```
Mouse motion at position ((702, 633)) with velocity ((-0.000042, 0.000042))
Mouse motion at position ((697, 635)) with velocity ((-0.000625, 0.00025))
```
But moving around and clicking with pen generates nothing.
[wayland_input_wacom.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/14284484/wayland_input_wacom.zip)

Video demonstration with game run with `display/display_server/driver.linuxbsd = wayland` option:
![recording.webm](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/54743395/d7eaa291-d709-4df6-81f8-2376c472712d)
When cursor is visible and data is printed, that's mouse.
When cursor become invisible, that's when I use pen on tablet.

When `display/display_server/driver.linuxbsd = default`, everything works fine:
![works_fine.webm](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/54743395/8977f51f-d487-4d88-b5d4-8a2cb0edff67)
First I move with mouse, then pen, then mouse again and then pen again. In all cases inputs are printed.
comments: I tested Huion H430P tablet without screen, and it also doesn't work. In fact, Godot didn't recognized any inputs from this tablet, including onboard buttons (there 4 in total).

Known issue. There was some very basic support once (which got blasted by a refactor) but as I don't have a fancy tablet (multiple tools, tilting) I can't really plumb some good enough support in the first place, sorry :(

Edit: to be clear, I can try doing some blind implementations and letting test stuff to somebody who has a fancy multi-tool tablet, but that would take some time. Would somebody be willing to do that?
Is there possibility to open some kind of fundraiser to buy tablet for testing?
@Riteo It might be worth trying https://github.com/H-M-H/Weylus with a phone/tablet. Its Wayland support is marked as experimental though.

> Is there possibility to open some kind of fundraiser to buy tablet for testing?

@Vovkiv I don't know. A multi-tool, tilt-enabled tablet would also cost a lot. I think that it might be a lot easier and cheaper to go backwards and forwards with somebody who has a proper multi-tool and tilt-aware tablet.

@Vovkiv after some very careful semi-blind coding, @winston-yallow's testing with their graphic tablet and some luck I think I managed to implement the thing :D

Please tell me if it works for you :)

@Riteo after some embarrassingly long time trying to figure how to compile Godot, I did it, yay!
Here result with `display/display_server/driver.linuxbsd = wayland`, test project seems to works without any issues on Wacom tablet:
![wayland_new_does_work.webm](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/54743395/42b2150f-5114-47c3-ac19-5ebd3457f7a0)

Without this pr it does nothing, as expected:
![old_doesnt_work](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/54743395/401e0f51-01af-4332-ba06-c67d180aabd5)

I can't test this with other tablet (huion that I mentioned earlier) for reasons that it magically vanished in time and space, but since Wacom works, I assume other tablets also will work as expected.

Also, Godot editor itself now works with `run/platforms/linuxbsd/prefer_wayland = true`.
